profile.headline: Software Engineer | Backend & Platform Infrastructure | Java · Spring Boot · AWS · Distributed Systems | Payments & Real-Time Fraud Decisioning
profile.summary:
I'm a software engineer with 6 years of experience building high-throughput, event-driven distributed systems, most recently on Intuit's payments platform.

At Intuit I designed and built core components of the Payment Processing Framework (PPF), which handles 3M+ daily transactions at 99.99% uptime: request validation, transaction authorization, and an SNS/SQS resiliency queue with automatic retries and idempotency. I owned workstreams in the Payments 1.0 to 2.0 migration that moved 100% of production traffic onto the new platform, and led Tap to Pay delivery as project owner, including Intuit's first Android Tap to Pay support. I also mentored junior engineers and drove production readiness: Splunk dashboards and alerts, on-call, and incident root-cause analysis.

Earlier, on Intuit's real-time fraud Decision Engine, I worked across the data layer behind ML-driven scoring, including Spark jobs over Kafka event streams, Python tooling for ML training datasets, and Elasticsearch and Cassandra lookups at sub-10ms p99. I also led the team's Identity 2.0 migration and disaster recovery work.

Outside Intuit, I co-founded Vibe Nexus and ship two live consumer apps, Influence: DJ Crowd Insights and Influence Karaoke.

I'm strongest in Java, Spring Boot, Kafka, AWS, Kubernetes, and distributed systems, and I use AI tools like Cursor and Claude Code day to day.

📍Los Angeles area (Lomita, CA) | adamstrejon@gmail.com

positions.title: Co-Founder / Software Engineer
positions.description:
• Engineered and maintain two React Native consumer applications, establishing a single JavaScript codebase to deliver seamless cross-platform performance across iOS and Android.

• Designed a real-time DJ dashboard using React Native, implementing efficient client-side state management for live request queues, multi-attribute sorting/filtering, batch actions, and dynamic data visualizations.

• Developed a lightweight React and TypeScript web app allowing audience members to seamlessly submit live song preferences, real-time vibe updates, and shoutout requests during sets.

• Created a serverless Node.js backend on GCP Cloud Run functions, designing a scalable Firestore NoSQL data model and securely integrating the Stripe API for payments and payouts and the Spotify API for track metadata retrieval.

• Built the full stack with React Native, Node.js, and Firebase, including a QR-launched web client and a real-time data model that aggregates live audience submissions into a dashboard DJs use during a set; integrated Stripe Connect and one-time payments for song requests and tips, plus the Spotify API.

positions.title: Software Engineer 2
positions.description:
• Owned multiple workstreams in the Payments 1.0 to 2.0 migration, including data parity validation, end-to-end testing, and phased rollouts with feature flags, moving 100% of production traffic onto the new platform.

• Designed and built three core components of Intuit's Payment Processing Framework (PPF), which handles 3M+ daily transactions at 99.99% uptime: request validation, transaction authorization, and an SNS/SQS sweeper and resiliency queue with automatic retries and idempotency, on Java/Spring Boot, AWS, and Kubernetes.

• Delivered Amex and JCB acceptance for Canadian merchants, PPF's first card-not-present flow, building the Payment Gateway REST integration and Kafka transaction events and setting patterns reused across Payments 2.0.

• Led Tap to Pay delivery in PPF as project owner and primary developer, routing 100% of Apple Tap to Pay traffic to Payments 2.0 with 0% data mismatch and building Intuit's first Android Tap to Pay support.

• Mentored 3 contractor engineers through architecture and code reviews, knowledge transfer, and cross-time-zone delivery planning.

• Built PCI-compliant card-present support in PPF, including card data decryption and EMV and swipe handling.

• Created Splunk dashboards and alerts across PPF and team services, drove operational readiness to 100% compliance on two services, and supported on-call root-cause analysis using Claude Code with MCP to query logs across services.

• Led incident response for an Amex Canada transaction issue in the resiliency sweeper, tracing the root cause, correcting affected transaction records, and adding regression tests to prevent recurrence.

• Analyzed three legacy services with Claude Code and produced the migration docs, technical specs, work estimates, and stories for moving their APIs onto Payments 2.0, adopted for the team's next quarterly planning.
positions.insights: Cross-functional Collaborations, Incident Management and +10 skills

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
• Maintained and extended Java/Spring Boot services for Intuit's Decision Engine, a low-latency rules- and ML-driven platform scoring fraud on millions of daily transactions in real time; secondary SME for its Enrichment service.

• Integrated Spark into the Decision Engine, computing risk features from high-volume Kafka event streams.

• Built Python validation tooling converting raw transaction features from the data lake into ML training datasets for the data science team's offline models.

• Contributed to the data serving layer for the real-time ML fraud engine, indexing millions of risk profiles in Elasticsearch, caching transaction state in Cassandra, and tuning queries to sub-10ms p99 lookups.

• Built the command layer of the team's BDD testing framework, making rule and policy test authoring self-service for the policy team; adopted by partner teams across the organization.

• Led the Identity 2.0 migration across every service the team owned, modernizing authentication to meet enterprise compliance standards, and implemented Data Governance 2.0 controls for the Enrichment service.

• Implemented disaster recovery across the Risk Vendor, Risk Analysis, and Rules Artifact Manager services, authored the team's DR plan, and built graceful cross-region failover for Kafka consumers between US East and West.
positions.insights: Cross-functional Collaborations, Incident Management and +11 skills

positions.title: Software Engineer I
positions.description:
• Contributed core functionality and Boost-based unit tests to a large-scale Python-to-C++ migration.

• Triaged and resolved defects with Coverity static analysis and peer-reviewed teammates' fixes.

• Served as Scrum Master, running sprint planning, demos, and retrospectives.

positions.title: Software Engineer Intern
positions.description:
- Created a graphical user interface for a general processing element (GPE) used on the windows server 2016 platform.
- Integrated my front-end development with back-end in order to properly execute modes within the application. 
- Utilized agile methodology with scrum by participating in daily stand-ups, bi-weekly sprints, and retrospectives to aid in product development.
- Generated requirements document, Formal Qualification Test (FQT), and user’s guide for the GPE Interface app.

positions.title: Student Technical Assistant
positions.description:
- Installed and maintain Windows and Mac operating Systems (OS).
- Provided support to users on a variety of IT related issues such as: network, printer, and software issues.
- Documented, tracked, and monitored problems to ensure that they are resolved in a timely manner.

company.name: University of California, Irvine School of Law

positions.title: Engineering Experience Mentor
positions.description:
Mentoring Position at a Summer Engineering Camp for elementary school students which allowed me to do the following things:

Collaboratively worked with my peers to instruct and manage a classroom of 3rd grade students.
Exposed students to STEM fields by teaching them a variety of hands-on engineering toys.
Instructed students on the engineering design process and general math and science concepts. 

The camp was sponsored by NSBE and ran for three weeks. I was on the job for a time span of four weeks.

volunteerExperiences.description: I prepared informational folders for students to read and spoke to them about the college experience regarding STEM and answered any questions that they may have had. I also guided students in creating their own computer program using a software called Scratch.

projects.title: Client-Server Chat Application
projects.description: A project in which we implemented multi-client/server communication by using socket programming and I/O multiplexing. We worked with GTK+ API to handle GUI and user input and output within the main program. CVS was used with other team members for organization and to maintain up to date source code. We applied our own test modules to aid in testing specific functions of the program like client-server connection.

projects.title: Chess in C
projects.description: A project that allowed us to implement data structures to keep track of player information, chess board, and rules of the game. We also worked with SDL API in order to design and implement GUI with main program. We utilized object-oriented programming ideas to incorporate basic rules and functions of chess. We were able to strengthen communication and collaboration skills by working on a medium-scaled project. Lastly, we competed with other student's chess program's AI and was able to win one game.
